purpose: Test whether external dynamical information, rather than fitted-model consistency or extra exposure, is the source of augmentation value; test whether first-order Hankel spectrum preservation itself changes the value of time warp.
literature_informed_novelty_target: fitted-model self-consistency as a forecasting-specific failure mode

lorenz.spectrum_projection: orthogonal trajectory-space projection onto kernel of the first-order source Hankel singular-value Jacobian, then rescale to the original time-warp movement

hyperparameter_policy.fixed_base_alpha: choose alpha using TRAIN and tuning split on the unaugmented base, then reuse for every arm; ridge only
hyperparameter_policy.retuned_alpha: choose alpha independently for each arm using TRAIN plus that arm and the tuning split; primary fair regularization comparison

lorenz.headroom_selection: defined only on the independent headroom calibration split using retuned hyperparameters; TEST is never used to decide eligibility

false_symmetry_equivalence.criterion: CI for mean test gain lies fully inside +/- band

fitted_model_equivalence.criterion: CI for mean test gain lies fully inside +/- band

spectrum_projection_equivalence.criterion: CI for paired difference in test gain between projected and ordinary time warp lies fully inside +/- band

success_criteria.oracle_diagnostic: oracle simulator should approach extra-real benefit; diagnostic, not a gate

interpretation_rules: Do not filter or redefine cells using TEST outcomes.
If fewer than 12 primary-learner seeds pass calibration headroom, declare the design underpowered/no-headroom and redesign rather than interpret synthetic nulls.
Do not describe fitted-model zero-update as universal: exact zero update requires generator and learner to coincide in representation and fitted map.
Residual alignment is diagnostic only and is not used to choose or generate candidates.
Anytime/betting confidence sequences are not part of this decisive batch gate.
